- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast tends to peak too early and then overcorrects downward, missing the true mean-reversion path.
- Model underestimates prices during sharp downward trends, particularly when true values dip below 65–68.
- Forecast shows persistent lag in recognizing true price momentum, especially in the 10–15 day horizon.
- Model exhibits “overshoot” behavior after price spikes — forecasts jump too high and then fall too fast, missing the true trough.
- Model fails to adjust for mean reversion in the 30-day window, often staying above true mean for too long.
- Forecast tends to be overly optimistic in the first 5–7 days after a spike, then gradually corrects — but too late.
- Model underestimates volatility in the final 5–7 days of the 30-day window, especially when true values show sharp declines.
- Forecast often ignores recent low values in the history window, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model exhibits “memory bias” — overweights recent high values and underweights recent low values in the 30-day window.
